ideas.title: Counterfactual branching oracle for step-level tool utility
ideas.problem_slice: No measurement exists of how much a step-wise policy can beat one pre-generation decision in dependent chains.
ideas.method: On training tasks, run the frozen model; at each decision point t fork two continuations (call tool now / do step directly), each continued by the fixed default policy, K=3 samples each. Label Delta_t = mean final correctness(call) - mean(no call). Oracle policies: (a) single-decision oracle choosing one action pattern per instance before generation, (b) step-wise oracle choosing per step with hindsight Delta_t. Compute U(lambda) and U-AUC for both.
ideas.experiment: When2Tool 3-hop envs (calculator/retriever/code) + HotpotQA subset with BM25; Qwen3-4B, Llama-3.1-8B. Metric: oracle U-AUC gap with bootstrap CI.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Step-wise oracle U-AUC exceeds single-decision oracle U-AUC by >= 2 points on at least one benchmark.

ideas.title: Two-head marginal-utility probe (MUP) on per-step hidden states
ideas.problem_slice: Need-probes predict whether a step is hard, not whether calling now changes the final outcome.
ideas.method: At decision point t take the last-token hidden states h_t (several layers, frozen backbone). Two logistic heads predict p_call(h_t) and p_nocall(h_t) of final correctness (labels from P1-C01 branching). Delta_hat = p_call - p_nocall. Act iff Delta_hat > lambda*c_k. One training run serves all lambda.
ideas.experiment: Same benchmarks; baselines: When2Tool single pre-generation probe, step-wise need probe (Probing-RAG-style label = current correctness), SeaKR-style uncertainty threshold, always/never call. Metric: U-AUC, missed/unnecessary per step.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: MUP has higher U-AUC than a step-wise need probe at matched features and data.

ideas.title: Regret-weighted decision-focused training of the step-wise call rule
ideas.problem_slice: Estimating two probabilities and subtracting them amplifies noise; decisions only need the sign of Delta_t - lambda*c.
ideas.method: Train a single scorer g(h_t, lambda*c_k) with a cost-sensitive classification loss whose target is sign(Delta_t - lambda*c_k) and weight |Delta_t - lambda*c_k| (regret weighting, adapted from CAM-DF to call/no-call). lambda sampled per example during training so one model covers all costs.
ideas.experiment: Compare with MUP (P1-C02) and need probe at matched data; metric U-AUC and regret per step.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Regret-weighted training lowers per-step decision regret vs two-head subtraction.

ideas.title: Fitted-Q call policy over probe features with continuation value
ideas.problem_slice: One-step lookahead ignores that calling early can make later calls unnecessary (or vice versa).
ideas.method: Treat the chain as an MDP with state features phi(h_t), remaining hops, calls so far. Offline fitted Q-iteration on logged branched trajectories with reward = correctness - lambda*sum cost; small MLP Q(phi, a, lambda). Frozen backbone.
ideas.experiment: 3-hop envs; compare to one-step MUP; metric U-AUC; ablate horizon.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Fitted-Q beats one-step rules only when hop errors propagate.

ideas.title: Learned re-evaluation gate: when to re-probe
ideas.problem_slice: Probing at every step adds overhead and false positives; most steps may not change the decision.
ideas.method: A tiny gate on (h_t - h_{t-1}) norm, step type and previous decision predicts whether the utility estimate can change; only then run the utility probe; otherwise reuse the last decision.
ideas.experiment: Measure probe invocations, latency, U-AUC vs probing every step.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Gating cuts probe calls by half with no significant U-AUC loss.

ideas.title: Conformal step-wise calling with a bounded missed-call rate
ideas.problem_slice: Thresholds give no guarantee on how often a necessary call is skipped.
ideas.method: Split-conformal calibration on the utility score: choose per-lambda threshold so that the trajectory-level rate of skipped calls with Delta_t > 0 is <= epsilon on exchangeable data.
ideas.experiment: Report empirical missed-call rate vs epsilon and U(lambda) cost of the guarantee.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Empirical missed-call rate stays <= epsilon while U drop vs uncalibrated rule is small.

ideas.title: Pre-generation probe cascade with step-wise fallback
ideas.problem_slice: When2Tool's single probe is already strong; step-wise probing may only matter for uncertain instances.
ideas.method: Run When2Tool-style probe at t=0; if |p - 0.5| > m, commit to its decision for all steps; else switch to step-wise utility probing.
ideas.experiment: U-AUC and overhead vs pure single and pure step-wise.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Cascade matches step-wise U-AUC with fewer probe evaluations.

ideas.title: Tool-conditioned shared utility probe with leave-one-tool-out transfer
ideas.problem_slice: Per-tool probes do not transfer; heterogeneous tools have different costs and reliabilities.
ideas.method: One probe with tool embedding (learned vector per tool) concatenated to h_t; train on two tools, test on the third.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Shared probe transfers above chance to the held-out tool.

ideas.title: Hop-local vs final-outcome step labels
ideas.problem_slice: Step labels can be defined by hop correctness or by final answer; which yields better decisions is unknown.
ideas.method: Train identical probes with (a) hop-local correctness labels and (b) final-outcome counterfactual Delta labels.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Final-outcome labels yield higher U-AUC on chains with error propagation.

ideas.title: Cost-shift robustness of a single cost-conditioned rule vs per-cost trained policies
ideas.problem_slice: The anchor trains one model per alpha; a single conditioned rule may degrade when costs move outside the training range.
ideas.method: Train utility rule on lambda in [0.1,0.4], test on [0.5,0.8]; compare to per-lambda trained probes.
ideas.experiment: U(lambda) curves in and out of range.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Single conditioned rule stays within CI of per-lambda probes out of range.

ideas.title: Per-step utility prior injected in context (CTA-style) vs prefill steering
ideas.problem_slice: How to act on a per-step estimate: force via prefill or let the model reason with the number.
ideas.method: At each step insert 'Estimated benefit of calling now: x; cost: y' (CTA-Prompted) vs When2Tool soft/hard prefill.
ideas.experiment: Same estimator, two actuation modes; U-AUC.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Prefill beats in-context priors for <= 8B non-thinking models.

ideas.title: Hidden-state vs token-probability features for step utility
ideas.problem_slice: Whether hidden states add information over cheap output probabilities at each step is unmeasured for tool utility.
ideas.method: Same utility labels; features = hidden states vs FLARE/DRAGIN-style token-probability statistics vs both.
ideas.hypothesis_sketch: Hidden states beat token-probability features at matched data.
